I hope, in next year''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''''s Budget speech, that is, 2006-07. probably, he would implement it. I have gone through the speeches of the first Finance Minister of India, Shri Chettiar, who is from Tamil Nadu. From the first Budget speech onwards I have gone through all the speeches of the Finance Ministers of India till last year. The Finance Minister has earmarked Rs.6,000 crore for the welfare of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes. 

16.00 hrs.

Last year, they spent Rs.600 crore. It costs Rs. 600 crore for laying a road from Delhi to Jaipur. They spent Rs.600 crore last year for Scheduled Castes. He had said that he would be spending Rs.6000 crore for Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes. I had mentioned about it in some other meeting. I have got the figures with me. The system can misguide the Finance Minister; the system can misguide the Prime Minister. But the system cannot misguide the Parliament. I have got records with me. I have the papers with me. I say this with all humility. I know, the hon. Finance Minister is looking at page 52, statement number 20. I have gone through each and every page of it. They have brought in nothing but the bundle of untruths. I went to the Department. I met the Section Officer. I met the Joint Secretary who is dealing with this subject. I met the Secretary. I request the Finance Minister to go back and do a little bit of home work and see that the Scheduled Castes, the Scheduled Tribes and the poor people of this country are benefited. I had hoped that my friends from the Left parties, from the BSP, would raise it. Shri Swain was criticising the Budget from the rooftop. Instead of that, had he raised this issue, we would have been glad. But, I am forced to speak on this from the Congress side because this is the need of the hour. I request the hon. Finance Minister to go through this. I have got the records. I am placing it on the Table of the House.

With this, I congratulate the Finance Minister and I congratulate the Prime Minister. They are going to bring revolution in this country. They are going to bring revolutionary changes in the rural economy. Today, the country is in a praiseworthy position. I was a bitter critic of reforms earlier. Today, I gladly say that our country is the third largest economy of Asia. The foreign exchange reserves of the country are in the fourth place in the world. With this, I congratulate the Government, I congratulate the Finance Minister. I request him to do something for the poor people.

* Sir, economy goes with politics. Economy and politics are interlinked. Before I get into the Budget, I would like to speak a little about the history and geo-political situation. I happen to go through the Budget delivered by the Finance Ministers since 1947. The first Budget was delivered by Shri Shanmugam Chettiar, who was the first Finance Minister of India. Later, it was 

* Speech was laid on the Table.

by John Mathai. In 1958, the Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru presented the Budget and said while replying the Budget: "Our economy must be open to the world and when the world changes we should also change. We should keep our eyes open to the world."

The second thing is that "when we present a Budget, we should keep in mind what the pedestrian is thinking, whether he is happy or not; but not the people who are travelling in cars. That is important." Later in 1970, the late PM, Shrimati Indira Gandhi presented the Budget giving a different direction to the economy. Later, in 1987, the late PM Shri Rajiv Gandhi presented the budget which was ‘socialistic’. Before 1990, we used to import oil and arms from Russia through rupee Rouble Agreement/Exchange. After the sudden collapse of Soviet Russia, we got in to foreign exchange crisis. We were not having even foreign exchange for a few days. At that juncture, due to geo-political problems and keeping the economic crisis in mind, the Congress Party in power changed the economic direction on 24th July, 1991. Dr. Manmohan Singh, as Finance Minister and the Congress Party in power, brought an economic revolution in the country, more particularly, in urban areas. After a gap of 8 years, Dr. Manmohan Singh has become the Prime Minister to lead the UPA Government. Shrimati Sonia Gandhi, Congress President and Chairperson of UPA, the Prime Minister Dr. Manmohan Singh, comrade Bardhan, comrade Surjeet and other constituents of UPA brought the common minimum programme. We all are aware of the contents of NCMP. The main problems today are four in number :

Hunger ;Joblessness; Disease; illiteracy; 

From this Budget, what we can discuss today is that how we can analyse that the poor man’s hunger is solved. The main Mid-day meal Programme was started earlier by the Congress Party in power in 1995. It was started in a few areas and by giving 100 grams of rice or wheat to the children who are going to the primary schools. It gives an incentive to their education. Hon. Finance Minister, in his Budget speech, said that there are 11 crore poor children in the 

primary schools who are getting the Mid-day meals, that is, 3 kg of rice per month per child. 

I would like to congratulate whole-heartedly the Finance Minister, the Prime Minister and the Chairperson of UPA for bringing this programme.

Forty years back, I happened to take the Mid-day meal. I personally know the problem. This quantity of 100 gms per day per child is not sufficient. I request the hon. Finance Minister and the Prime Minister and the Chairperson of UPA to raise this quantity from 100 gms to 150 gms per day, which comes to four-and-a-half kgs of rice instead of 3 kg, per month, also cook charges from Re 1 to Rs.2 per child per month. Please name this Mid day meal after Rajiv Gandhi.

Secondly, the Finance Minister took some laudable steps and brought ICDS and Anganwadi centres. Again, this programme was brought by Shrimati Indira Gandhi and Congress Party in 1975. Today, 8, 37,000 Anganwadi centres are there. The UPA Government is giving nutritious food to 1 crore pregnant women and immunization to approximately 4 crore children between the age 0 to 6 years of age group.

I request the hon. Finance Minister to include 1 crore more pregnant women in this programme and name this programme after the name of Shrimati Indira Gandhi.

Thirdly, very important programmes like Antodhaya Anna Yojana was brought on 25th December, 2000 by the Opposition Party to help the poorest of the poor and the same programme, the hon. Finance Minister announced, that is, 35 kilos of wheat and 35 kilos of rice at the rate of Rs.2 and Rs.3 per kg, to remove the starvation from this country. This programme is to reach minimum two-and-a-half crore people in the country. This is one of the best programmes. I congratulate the Prime Minister and the Finance Minister and the Chairperson of the UPA and UPA constituents. To spell this Anna Antodhaya Yojana Scheme is difficult so as to make it easier to pronounce, I request the Government to announce the Programme in the name of BTR Yojana. You may ask about the BTR. It is nothing but comrade BT Rana Devae who was the founder of the Communist Movement in the country. 

I am sitting in Congress party. I strongly recommend this BTR Yojana. This is the major programme brought in by the Congress Party and the Minister to remove the hunger.

Next is about joblessness. Our main problem is no work and no food. There are 4 crore educated unemployed people in this country waiting for jobs since ages. In 2001, the Finance Minister, Shri Yashwant Sinha announced in his Budget Speech, recommended optimisation. Every year, in the Government of India, 1,20,000 people are retiring. Instead of filling the job vacancies, he stopped 80,000 jobs in a year. Only, 40,000 jobs are filled. There is a big gap between the jobs and the educated unemployed people in this country. There are 4 crore people waiting for jobs. By going for optimisation, the educated unemployed who are poor and who cannot get jobs in private sector are losing hope. This is turning towards inducement and unlawful activities. That is why maoism, drug addiction are increasing in this country. I request UPA government and Hon. Finance Minister to scrap this recruitment optimization order of 2001 brought by Shri Yashwant Sinha.

To create new jobs Finance Minister is bringing food for work programme in 150 districts and creating new jobs in Textile industry by bringing Rs. 30,000 crores of capital and incentives to construction industry. We are going to get 70 lakh jobs. This is a very praiseworthy. 

Next coming to diseases, to remove diseases, an amount of Rs.10,000 crores have been earmarked for health. All PHCs and sub-centres, district headquarters hospitals are all to be provided with doctors and medicines. The PM and the Finance Minister are going to build temple of health in all important centers in India, like AIIMS-like hospitals. All these are going to be temples of health in India. Instead of building such temple of health, our friends on the opposite side wanted to build temple in Ayodhya, which is very difficult today to discuss.

Coming to education, the Finance Minister have earmarked Rs.18,000 crore out of which Rs.4000 crore coming to building primary schools in the country. 1968, 1986, 1992 educational policies were announced. In every village, there is primary school, high school and in every important place, there is a college and a professional college. These are temples of education. From primary school to universities, we are going to have. This is the creation of the Congress-led UPA Government. In this way, Congress Party and UPA Government are bringing revolution in the rural economy. Today we are proud to say, India is the third largest economies in Asia, and the 4th largest foreign exchange reserves in the world.

Coming to housing, Indira Awas Yojana, with full subsidy 15 lakh houses are coming. Coming to Bharat Nirman, in four years, the Government is planning to irrigate one crore hectare of land for the poor people. It would also provide electricity, telephones, drinking water to all villages, roads in all villages. Some friends from opposite side were asking us in 47 years, so that Congress has done for Bharat Nirman. I wanted to tell our friends on the opposite, Congress has brought freedom to the country, Congress has brought good Constitution to the country. Congress brought democracy. Even in countries like Russia, China, Pakistan, they do not have democracy. Congress brought Green Revolution and economic revolution in this country. Today ours is the 3rd largest country in Asia.

Coming to the Scheduled Castes, the Finance Minister has said that he is bringing 6000 crore, at page 52 of Expenditure, Volume I, this shows the Government is little dull with the welfare of Scheduled Castes. Here, I agree. In all areas, the Finance Minister did very well, but not to the Scheduled Castes. In the last budget speech, he said, his heart is nearer to Scheduled Castes and Tribes. But this year 2005-06 budget, he did not show it. That itself is an eye opener to us. My friends opposite side and Left Parties should have asked the Finance Minister, if they are really concerned about it. Now, I am doing their duty and request the Finance Minister to discuss again with the Department and rectify the 

mistake that was done last year and this year also. I am not an expert in economics like them. 

But, I know the basics how tactfully our system can misguide the hon. Finance Minister and hon. Prime Minister and also the Parliament. Road from here to Jaipur costs Rs.600 crore. The same amount of Rs.600 crore was spent on SCs, from Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. And this year also it has said Rs.6000 crore for SCs and STs. This figure is wrong. You can say that the money is for SCs, STs, OBCs and other specific sections. Then I not say it is for SCs and STs. So, anyway, I congratulate hon. Finance Minister, hon. Prime Minister and hon. Chairperson of UPA from the core of my heart for bringing such a beautiful Budget, which, I have not seen in 57 years. Congress Party and UPA constituents are going to bring change in the country. 

In 1958, Pt. Jawahar Lal Nehru while replying to the debate for his Budget speech said, "Whenever we present the Budget, we should feel what the pedestrians are thinking about it." Hence, I would like to tell you what they are thinking. A person who is eating the rice with chutney wanted a dal curry and a person who is taking rice with dal curry wanted to eat rice with egg. A person who is sleeping on the floor wanted to sleep on a mat and a person who is sleeping on a mat wanted to sleep on a mattress. 

Today what is happening is that the gap between the rich and poor is widening. We have to reduce this gap and in "Bharat Nirman Project", in the coming 4 years, I hope we will be able to reduce the gap between the rich and the poor. Thus, only we can build this society which is an inclusive society.

By building "Bharat Nirman", I request the hon. Finance Minister to keep in mind that the gap between the poor and the rich is widening.

With this I conclude.

*SHRI S.K. KHARVENTHAN (PALANI): I am thanking our hon. Finance Minister, Shri P. Chidambaram for the presentation of a populist Budget. The Father of the Nation dreamed for Grama Rajya after freedom. Our Finance Minister dedicated this Budget for Grama Rajya. 

I want to elicit certain salient features of this Budget :

tax bracket altered;

tax exemption up to 1 lakh; 

for women and senior citizens up to 1.5 lakh income tax exemption;

from Rs. 1 lakh to 1.5 lakh tax will be 10%;

from Rs. 1.5 lakh to 2.5 lakh tax will be 20%;

beyond 2.5 lakh income, tax will be 30 per cent;

allocation of RS. 3,644 crore for Tsunami victims;

no customs duty on LPG and kerosene;

non-agricultural product tax reduced to 15 per cent;

textile machinery and refrigerated vans duty was reduced from 20 percent to 10 per cent;

Food processing - reduced from 20 per cent to 10 per cent in refrigerated vans;

Cooking coal duty reduced to 5 per cent;

polyesters and nylon chips, textile fibres, yarns, intermediates, fabrics and garments duty reduced to 15 per cent from 20 per cent;

excise duty on imitation and jewelry was cut down to 8 per cent;

surcharge and excise duty on tea, refined edible oil, and vanaspati abolished;

* Laid on the Table.

Customs duty on crude petroleum to be reduced from 10 per cent 5 

per cent;

Service tax exemption to them whose gross turnover does not exceed Rs. 4 lakh per year;

Further, present budget is aimed at to develop the rural infrastructure. For the successful implementation of the National Common Minimum Programme, in the present Budget Rs. 74,849.46 crore are allocated. For the rural development alone, Rs. 22,682.26 crore are allocated. For Sampoorna Gramin Rozgar Yojana and for National Food for Work Programme alone Rs. 9,000 crore are allocated. Whether this amount will reach the poor, down-trodden people. The identification of these works is totally based on the recommendations of State politicians. The foodgrains are not reaching the poor. It is being sold outside to market by the contractors. For Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana, Rs.3,809.50 is allocated. In Tamil Nadu, previously, the PMGSY road programmes were executed by panchayat unions, but now it is being taken up by Highways Departments. For the past one year, in my constituency, a number of works have not been started. The money allotted to these schemes is lying with the State Government. Under Area Development Programme for Rashtriya Sam Vikas Yojana – Backward Districts/Area, a Fund of Rs. 5,000 crore is allocated. My constituency, Palani, comes under the Dindigul District. It has been announced as one of the Backward Districts. For the year 2004-05, Rs. 15 crore were allocated, and for the year 2005-06, Rs. 15 crore are allocated. Last year, out of Rs. 15 crore, Rs. 124.310 lakh were allocated to Watershed Development Works through EE Agricultural Engineering but total Fund is misutilized. The above Department had not executed any programme properly in my constituency. In the same manner, for District Forest Office Dindigul and Kodaikanal, Rs. 145.450 lakh were allocated. For connectivity to forest villages Rs. 45 lakh were allocated. Under this Programme Ayyaloor in Vadamadurai Block to Senthurai in Natham Block were taken up, but 

the work is not yet completed. The work executed is also not proper. Huge money is swallowed by certain corrupt officials. If the method of selecting contractor, and the execution of work is verified, it will clearly prove the mis-management. Severe action is to be taken against the Forest official, who is executing the work. 

The works allotted to Agricultural Engineering Department, and Dindigul Forest Department under RSYV Scheme has to be thoroughly checked. Otherwise, allocation of huge amount by our Government is a total colossal waste.

Under RSYV Scheme, I repeatedly requested the District Forest Officer, Dindigul to include the connectivity to forest villages L. Malaiyar, P. Malaiyar in Natham Taluk, but no response is there till date. In this hilly region, people are struggling hard to reach hospital or market or town or for any urgent purpose without road. Most of the pregnant women were died before reaching hospital since they are taken by cot or by men. Road facility is very essential for the above hilly area.

Moreover, I want to congratulate the hon. Finance Minister for giving importance to rural education. For Sarva Shiksha Abiyan in 2004-05, Rs.3,057 crore were allocated, and for the current year, Rs. 4,754 crore are allocated. For ‘Prarambhik Shiksha Kosh", Rs. 7,156 crore are allocated. For Mid-day meal scheme, Rs. 1,675 crore were allocated during 2004-05, and for the current year, Rs. 7,156 crore are allocated. For the first time, for SC/ST students – those studying M.Phil and Ph.D - ‘Rajiv Gandhi National fewllowship" is created, and it has been decided to give Rs. 2000 fellowship per year. For Agricultural Marketing and Diversification, Rs. 2,283.28 crore is allocated. In the last Budget, our hon. Finance Minister allocated a huge fund for Agricultural Loans and Education loans, but some of the banks are wantonly avoiding to give loans to farmers and students. The Government announced 5 years time for payment of co-operative loans, but some of the Nationalized banks insist farmers to clear the co-operative loans and get no-objection certificates. Even though our hon. Finance Minister visited a number of banks and instructed the bank officials, yet they are not adhering to the orders of the Government. 

Furthermore, I humbly request the hon. Finance Minister to consider the pathetic situation of the Indian farmers. In the North India, farmers are struggling due to heavy flood, and in South India farmers are struggling without water. The Government has to fund for inter-linking rivers at least for South Indian rivers.

Moreover, Government has to consider sympathetically the pathetic position of the poor farmers, and at least the Government has to waive off the interest and penal interest payable by the poor farmers to the co-operative institutions.

The hon. Finance Minister is a senior advocate, and a legal luminary in this country. He better knows the position of courts in rural area. Particularly courts in Taluk area are in very poor condition. For example, in my constituency, and in Kangayam town, Munsif and Magistrate courts are functioning in a cattle shed. Like-wise, the Vedashenthur Court is functioning in a dilapidated old dwelling house. This is the situation throughout the country. A special fund has to be created for the infrastructural facilities for the rural courts in this country by our Government. 

Moreover, I want to mention about service tax. Particularly, the lorries that are taking foodgrains - paddy, wheat, rice and other foodgrains – be exempted. Otherwise, it will affect the common men.

In the last budget, our hon. Finance Minister announced to adopt Anand Model for purchase of horticultural products. This has to be extended to medicinal plants, and its extracts. For example, in Tamil Nadu, agriculturists are cultivating "Glorisa Superba". From "Superba" extracts are taken, and imported abroad. From farmers, only a few people are purchasing "Superba" seeds for Rs. 300 per kilo, and are exporting abroad for huge money. So many farmers died due to this cultivation. On considering the pathetic situation of farmers, Union of India has to purchase from the farmers like Anand Model, and save them.

With these words, I am supporting the Budget, 2005-06.

*DR. THOKCHOM MEINYA (INNER MANIPUR): Sir, I would put this Budget as one of the most balanced one in so far as our country is concerned where majority of the population is below poverty line. The introduction to the speech very clearly spelt out its contents-very precise and inclusive. The whole exercise is completed in as many as a dozen segments.

Sir, I would start my discussion by quoting Para 183 of the Finance Minister’s Speech: "This Budget is an attempt to lay down a path in which growth and equity will reinforce each other and build a new India." This is the theme with which the Finance Minister works to turn into action the agendum of the National Common Minimum Programme of the United Progressive Alliance led by the Indian National Congress. 

Sir, let me try to convince the hon. Members of this august House that this Budget is people friendly, poor friendly and in the process, it maintains the equilibrium among growth, stability and equity. While doing so, this Budget very clearly translates the address of His Excellency, the President of India to the Parliament into a perfect programme in words and in spirit. For this I wholeheartedly congratulate the hon. Finance Minister. Let us give him a big hand. 

Sir, the assault on poverty and unemployment clearly attempts to empower the people by initiating many schemes or missions. I would like to mention a few of them like rejection of the idea of jobless growth, National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme, National Rural Health Mission, Antyodaya Anna Yojana, Integrated Child Development Services, Mid-day Meal Scheme, Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan, Rajiv Gandhi National Drinking Water Mission, Total Sanitation 

* Speech was laid on the Table.

Campaign, separate statement on schemes for the development of SCs and STs, particularly, in the Education Sector by providing incentives or scholarships in large numbers, in institutes of excellence and Rajiv Gandhi National Fellowship for pursuing M.Phil and Ph.D. courses on the pattern of UGC fellowships.

Sir, gender budgeting, increasing the equity support for the National Minorities Development and Finance Corporation, opening of new schools under the Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan, as well as, the Kasturba Balika Vidyalaya Scheme and opening of new anganwadi centres in districts having a substantial minority population and development of Urdu in Uttar Pradesh and implementing schemes for pre-examination coaching of candidates belonging to the minority communities for competitive examinations by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment and the Ministry of Human Resource Development, Backward Region Grant Fund, special economic packages for Bihar, Jammu and Kashmir and the North Eastern Region, and the Rural Infrastructure Development Fund. 

Sir, the implementation of the Udhampur-Baramulla rail line in Jammu and Kashmir as a project of national importance; supporting the Kumarghat-Agartala Lamding-Silchar-Jiribam-Imphal projects with additional funds outside the Railway Budget as projects of national importance and approval of a special package for highway development in the North Eastern Region, show the keenness on the part of the Government to eliminate the regional imbalances apparently existing in the country. 

Sir, I wholeheartedly join my hon. friends in the Treasury Bench to complement His Excellency, the President of India for his overarching vision called ‘Bharat Nirman’ to build India and the hon. Finance Minister for making it a business plan comprising of six components, namely, irrigation, roads, water supply, housing, rural electrification and rural telecom connectivity. The most encouraging part of this gigantic plan lies in its commitment to fully involve the Panchayati Raj Institutions in the planning and implementation. 

Sir, in our country, with two thirds of the population dependent on agriculture and the sector producing only 21 per cent of the GDP in 2003-04, the Government rightly proposes to enhance public-private participation in investment in the infrastructure required to support expansion, diversification and value addition. Whereas in the industrial sector, both the public sector and the private sector are to be allowed the space to grow and compete with each other. In order to achieve this, a number of projects or schemes are proposed for implementation. I would like to mention a few of them like Roadmap for Agricultural Diversification, National Horticulture Mission, Massive Re-plantation and Rejuvenation, Development and Strengthening of Agricultural Marketing Infrastructure through agencies like National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD), National Cooperative Development Corporation (NCDC) and Agricultural Produce Marketing Committee (APMC).

Sir, the initiation of national projects for repair, renovation and restoration of water bodies; Proper and effective flood management in the states of Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, West Bengal, Orissa, Assam and North Eastern States; Implementation of Accelerated Irrigation Benefit Programme (AIBP); Micro Irrigation; Regularization of Rural Credit and Indebtedness; Making Cooperative Banks in India to comply with Section 11 of the Banking Regulation Act 1949; Farm Insurance; Micro Finance; Micro Insurance; Establishment of a Knowledge Centre in every village in the country and recognition of the vital role of agricultural research in the present day environment; to take special care required for an agricultural land like ours. 

Sir, the Budget suggests a number of infrastructural development programmes. The National Highway Development Project, Rural Electrification, Indira Awas Yojana, Special Purpose Vehicle, Provision of Urban Amenities in Rural Areas (PURA), National Urban Renewal Mission are worth mentioning. 

Sir, in the financial sector, the Minister has set things to the right direction and has tuned properly by balancing Banking, Capital Market, Over the Counter Derivatives, Stamp Duty on Stock Exchange Corporatization and Commercial Paper, Making a Regional Financial Centre at Mumbai and by introducing Gold Units. The setting up of a Pension Fund Regulatory Authority is going to do a lot of good to the needy. This Government is able to meet the extra burden expected to follow while implementing the Twelfth Finance Commission recommendations. Anyway, states are going to gain by the award of the Commission. 

Sir, in implementing the NCMP, the Government requires a huge amount of money for which resource mobilization is the only way out. Hence, the result is tax proposals. While welcoming the tax proposals put forward in the Budget, which are quite balanced in both Indirect Tax and Direct Tax fronts, there appears to be a common wish everywhere to request the Finance Minister not to levy the 0.1 per cent tax on withdrawal of cash on a single day of over Rs.10,000 or more from banks. I also very humbly wish that there should not be such a levy anyway.

Finally, Sir, I beg to join my esteemed friends in the Treasury Bench to support this Budget 2005-06, which is by far one of the most balanced Budget.

*SHRI J.M. AARON RASHID (PERIYAKULAM): Sir, at the outset, I would like to state that it is a matter of privilege to be part of the United Progressive Government which has started on the right lines. There is no denying of the fact that the United Progressive Alliance Government would complete its full term and would bounce back to power with wider mandate.

This Government has made great strides in every conceivable field. Be it agriculture, education, health, power.

This Government is bound to make great strides in every conceivable field under the stewardship of Dr. Manmohan Singh and under the able guidance of Smt. Sonia Gandhi, who has made great sacrifice by not accepting the Prime Ministership in spite of the clear mandate.

Ours is not a marriage of convenience like earlier NDA Government, ours is a marriage of consensus which is going to continue for a longer period than expected by the Opposition.

Hike in petroleum has resulted in overall price increase. Central Government should come out with a formula which would help to stop the hike in petroleum products. 

Of course, a number of problems have to be addressed by the Central Government. Namely, water, population explosion, health for all, power, floods, et al. It has just started its work. It has a long way to go.

The stark reality is that in India water problem would continue to haunt us as long as we depend on monsoon. We should develop a fool-proof rain harvesting system in each and every household to solve the problem of water. Another solution lies in the linking of rivers which is a stupendous and arduous task which can be implemented only by pooling enormous money. I do not 

* Speech was laid on the Table.

actually know whether it is feasible. But I am all the more certain that I would take long years to complete the linking of rivers. But if we complete this unthinkable task, our future generations would have a sigh of relief. Central Government has to study afresh the problems being faced in the implementation of linking or rivers, at least, we can erect check dams in every 2 kms. on river waterways.

I would like to point out here that every year we discuss a multifarious issues, namely, floods, droughts, railway accidents, etc. Discussing such issues has become a sort of ritual every year. The outcome is not worth appreciative for reasons known to everyone. We take up issues piecemeal and go about sorting out the immediate problems but forgetting about chalking out a well thought out plans and programmes to cater to the needs of each and every impending issue that come up often and in every year. We have to fix our sight in resolving issues that crop up every year on a permanent basis.

I would like to point out here in this august House the plight of farmers in Tamil Nadu, in particular. A number of farmers have been facing problems due to shortage of water, difficulties in getting loans, etc. Government should waive all the pending loans and allow the farmers to start the life afresh. I am of the firm conviction that as long as we depend on monsoon, we are bound to face such problems. Waived off thousands of crores of rupees to save the farmers is in the interest of the country. Given free power to the small farmers would go a long way in increasing the production. 

Stopping population explosion should be the immediate task of the Central Government. We could not move ahead as fast as we can in spite of our achievements in various fields because our ever increasing population is standing in the way of our country’s glory in the comity of nations.

Health is one are in which India’s position is not worthy of mention. Though we have made great strides in the field of health, according to a report, more than 26 crores people cannot afford healthcare and the Government hospitals cater to only a quarter of the people who approach the Government hospitals desperately without any source of treatment. Government hospitals should be upgraded in par with the state of the art private hospitals.

Funds should be extended generously to the schools run by Wakf Boards all over the country in general and Tami Nadu in particular. Due to acute shortage of funds, schools under the aegis of Wakf Boards are in a pitiable condition. I hope Government would give utmost priority to this aspect to help the minority community to keep pace with the advancements made in other schools, particularly urdu schools.

Education is another area, where we have to lay more emphasis in the years to come. Dropouts from schools have not reduced over the years. Innovative and effective steps should be made to ensure that each and every child, particularly from the underprivileged sections of the society and people living in despicable conditions attend the school. If we provide education to one and all, there is no doubt that our country would become a developed country sooner rather than later.

Tamil Nadu has a huge tourism potential. It should be tapped from every sense of word. Tourism is an area where we can bring in more foreign exchange. Maintenance of historical sites along with improvement of infrastructure with low budget hotels, airports facilities and rail services would undoubtedly improve the inflow of foreigners. Government should look into this aspect with insight and should come out with immediate steps to set right the way for more inflow of foreign tourists into our country, particularly Tamil Nadu, we have Ooty, Kaojikandal, Yercaud, Yelagiri Hills, Bodimottu.

I would like to suggest that a model school be set up in each district of the country; centres providing health care particularly to be needy and poorest of the poor should be started in the nook and corner of the country; proper roads should be laid in the remotest areas of the country so that people living in those areas would become part of the national mainstream. 

Power is another subject which is to be treated with utmost seriousness. Power thefts should be stopped lock stock and barrel. All-out efforts should be made to use the renewable sources of energy like wind and solar energy to tide over the huge shortage of electricity in various parts of the country.

Unemployment is one of the gravest problems India is facing not only today but for years. New thrust should be given by the UPA Government to take the problem of unemployment with all the seriousness it deserves. Employment generation is to be given top priority. Jawahar Rozgar Yojana should be taken up with more vigour. It should be reviewed to see that whether it is moving on the right lines.

The UPA Government should strengthen the Panchayati Raj Institutions to see that the real fruits reach the people at the bottom for whom it is meant. Here, I would like to quote late Rajiv Gandhi, who said that only 10 per cent reaches the public and the balance 90 per cent is siphoned off by the middlemen. This trend should be set right.

The UPA Government should strengthen the Panchayati Raj Institutions to see that the real fruits reach the people at the bottom for whom it is meant. Here, I would like to quote late Rajiv Gandhi, who said that only 10 per cent reaches the public and the balance 90 per cent is siphoned off by the middlemen. This trend should be set right.

When I was curiously going through the debates of the House and also the reports of various committees, I have found out to my astonishment that a considerable percentage of the grant or funds are not utilised in a particular year. This despicable situation must change if we want to see a bright future for India. We should ensure that funds are spent in full in a given year by planning in advance and executing well in time thereby spending the grant meant to be spent in a given year.

Mid-day meal scheme which is in vogue in a few States should be introduced at the national level to bring more people to school and which would provide at least a meal a day to those who could not make both ends meet or get a square meal a day. Central Government should extend grants generously so that we could improve the literacy of the country like the one in Kerala which has 100 per cent literacy. Any country which has its considerable population educated would undoubtedly make strides in every conceivable area.

Tamil Nadu has been facing the problem of water almost every year. Central Government should extend financial assistance to tide over the recurring problem every year. Protected water to be given to all rural public without fluoride content.

We have to take innovative and corrective steps. It would not be right on my part to outline what the Government should do as I have just started my Parliamentary life. I have a long way to go. But I am doubly sure that his Government would bring back the glorious days of governance of Jawaharlal Nehru, Indira Gandhi and Rajiv Gandhi who took India to great heights.

*SHRI E.G. SUGAVANAM (KRISHNAGIRI): Sir, first of all, I would like to express my gratitude to our great leader, hon. Dr. Kalaignar Karunanidhi and Thalapathi, M.K. Stalin for sending me to this august House. The Budget has been welcomed by all sections of the society although with certain minor reservations.

I have a few specific points to make regarding the budgetary proposals and put forth my suggestions and demands. First of al, I understand that it is under consideration of the Government to set up 6 AIIMS like institutions throughout the country. But, no such institution is being set up in Tamil Nadu. I would like to request that one such institution is going to be set up in Tamil Nadu at a suitable location to cater to 6.5 crore people of the State. It is because the facilities in the State Government hospitals are not sufficient and the private hospitals charge heavy fees and they do not provide any quality healthcare.

The Mid-Day Meal Scheme for Children is a very welcome proposal. At present, the Government is providing foodgrains at the rate of Re. 1 per child. With the rise in general prices and inflationary trend, the amount allotted is very less. I would like to request that, at least, it should be increased to Rs. 3 per child.

In the Rajiv Gandhi National Drinking Water Mission, importance has been laid on tackling water quality in about many thousands of habitations in Andhra Pradesh, Gujarat, Karnataka, Rajasthan, West Bengal and other States. I am sorry to stay that the quality of drinking water in the districts, namely, Dharmapuri and Krishnagiri is very poor and contains high rate of fluoride. Therefore, I would like 

*Speech was laid on the Table.

to request that adequate financial assistance should be given under the Rajiv Gandhi National Drinking Water Mission for providing protected water to the people of my constituency.

Sir, Dharmapuri and Krishnagiri Districts are facing acute shortage of water and groundwater level has also come down considerably. During the earlier Government, when Dr. Kalaignar was the Chief Minister, a scheme was inaugurated for Integrated Drinking Water Project in Hogenekal at a cost of Rs. 1,000 crore with Japanese assistance, and all modalities were worked out. However, the present Government has not taken any steps to implement the project and kept it in cold storage. I urge upon the Government to allocate adequate financial assistance for implementing the scheme on a war-footing level.

Sir, my next point is regarding the announcement of funds for backward districts. I understand that 170 backward districts have been identified. Dharmapuri and Krishnagiri Districts are the most backward Districts in Tamil Nadu. There are no major industries here and as such there are no employment opportunities. Since there is no adequate water supply, the agricultural operations have been affected and people are forced to migrate to other States. Therefore, I urge upon the Government to declare the above two Districts as backward Districts, and adequate financial assistance should be given for the development of these two Districts.

Sir, the proposal regarding pre-examination coaching of candidates belonging to the minority communities to allow them to pursue their courses in reputed private coaching institutions is a welcome step. But, this facility should be extended to the people belonging to Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, Other Backward Classes and economically weaker sections.

Sir, the National Horticulture Mission is being launched in April, 2005. Plenty of fruits and flowers are grown in Dharmapuri and Krishnagiri Districts. Therefore, a special package for these two Districts under the National Horticulture Mission should be allocated. In fact, the Finance Ministry should recommend to the Commerce Ministry for setting up of dry port in Krishnagiri Constituency for exporting fruits, vegetables and flowers to different areas within the country and abroad.

The National Water Project on Water Bodies is limited to 16 districts only. I would like to request that this project should be extended to Tamil Nadu and, in particular, to Dharmapuri and Krishnagiri Districts.

Sir, as the hon. Finance Minister is very well aware that Tamil Nadu is one of the leaders in handloom sector. But the export in this sector has dwindled in the past few years. Therefore, special steps should be taken to revive the sector and to increase the exports. Moreover, the life and health insurance packages should be extended to all weavers.

Sir, regarding the small-scale industrial sector, if more and more items are de-reserved, the small-scale industrial sector will not be able to compete with multinational companies. So, I would like to request the Government to give a serious thought before de-reserving any item from the small-scale industrial sector.

Sir, as I had already started that Dharmapuri and Krishnagiri are backward districts and they should be included under the ‘National Food for Work Programme’. The housing scheme for weaker sections in my constituency is not much and adequate allocations should be made under the Indira Awas Yojana.

Now, I turn my attention to taxation proposals. The proposal to impose surcharge on withdrawal of more than Rs. 10,000/- on a single day has not been appreciated by majority of the population of the country. In fact, our leader, Dr. Kalaignar has also expressed his reservation against this move. Therefore, I would like to request the Government to withdraw this proposal immediately. Due to this proposal, the black money cannot be curbed. In fact, the black money will increase, as people will tend to keep money with them and not deposit it in banks.

Hosur, which is an important centre, is located in my constituency. It is very nearer to Bangalore – the computer capital of India. There is plenty of possibility for setting up of software industries and companies, as it would create employment opportunities for the people in my constituency.

I request to grant special funds required by the 
 State Government.

Sir, once again, I compliment the UPA Government and Finance Ministry for presenting pro-people, pro-farmer budget for the welfare of all the sections of the society particularly the Backward communities, SC/STs and Minorities.

They have given the report but the Government is not implementing those recommendations. Again, they have appointed one Committee for holding discussion with the State Governments. This will not serve the purpose of the cooperative sector. 

Regarding the Accelerated Irrigation Benefit Programme, this Government has earmarked Rs.4600 crore in this year’s Budget. How is it possible to complete the pending 400 projects? I am asking this Government to react. There are 400 major and medium irrigation projects which are there to be completed. About 50 per cent of the work has been done. There is no money with the State Governments. That is why, they are not completing the projects. It requires Rs.20,000 crore to complete the 400 pending irrigation projects. But the Government has earmarked only Rs.4600 crore. This amount is not at all sufficient. Out of this amount also, the Government is giving 80 per cent as loan to the State Governments and the subsidy portion is only 20 per cent.

We are talking about agriculture and even the farming community. So, this is the situation. That is why, the Indian farmer is committing suicide. Even for the health sector, in the last Budget also, I proposed that there should be a Corpus Fund. The poor people in the villages cannot afford medical treatment. They are not getting assistance even from the Prime Minister’s Relief Fund. Some State Governments like the Karnataka Government formulated a Corpus Fund of Rs.100 crore or Rs.200 crore. Out of the accrued interest, they are providing some money to the poor people for meeting the expenses in connection with major, chronic diseases. I am requesting the hon. Finance Minister that he should create a Corpus Fund at the national level with a sum of Rs.1000 crore. Out of that, if you get something, then you can pass it on to the poor people. They are dying because of lack of money. This is the situation in the country. 

We are talking about stock market and everything. If the stock market falls, the whole Government is paying attention. But thousands of farmers are dying and we are not paying attention to them. How many people participated in the stock market operations? In the whole country, it is only 9 per cent. For example, you take the case of my village. From there, no person has invested money in the shares. Of course, in the European countries, in the USA, 95 per cent of the people are investing in stock market. Everybody is talking about stock market. But, in India, 75 per cent of the farmers are living in the rural villages. They have no link with the stock market and everything. If farmers are not getting the Minimum Support Price, nobody is talking about it. If farmers commit suicide, nobody is talking. This is the scenario prevailing in the country. 

I am giving one small example. I come to the Tobacco Board. The farmers have accumulated Rs.100 crore of money to the Tobacco Board. Even the tobacco farmers are not getting the Minimum Support Price in Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka. The farmers are crying. It is their own money. The sum of Rs.100 crore is the cess. That is the farmers’ own money. The Government is not releasing the money to intervene in the market to purchase tobacco. These are our policies. We are not requesting the Government of India to provide some money. We are not asking the Government of India, the STC to intervene in the market for the purchase of tobacco. But the farmers have accumulated Rs.100 crore of money with the Tobacco Board. Even the Government of India is not giving permission to the Tobacco Board to intervene in the market to purchase tobacco. These are the policies.

How will the Indian farmers get benefit? Our farmers are small and marginal farmers. Eighty per cent of the farmers are small and marginal farmers. Now, they have to compete with the world markets. After the World Trade Organisation (WTO), we have to face the challenges throughout the world.

MR. DEPUTY-SPEAKER: Please conclude.

SHRI KINJARAPU YERRANNAIDU : We have to compete with the world. If the farmers are happy, then the whole India is happy. Then only, we can say that the Budget is a good Budget. We have to think about the farming community. Otherwise, there is no meaning of this Budget. It is all right that we are providing money to every sector. What is the use of it? Our colleagues, our fathers, our brothers and our sisters are dying. We are not providing any help to them. 

The hon. Finance Minister has increased the credit from Rs. 1,05,500 crore to Rs. 1,08,000 crore. I would like to give you one example about the nationalised banks, private banks and everything. Now, coming to the public sector banks, in the year 2001, only four banks achieved the target of 18 per cent, while 23 banks were failed to achieve this target. In the year 2002, only six nationalised banks achieved the target of 18 per cent, while 21 banks had not achieved the same target. In the year 2003, only five banks achieved the target of 18 per cent, while 22 banks had not achieved any success on this front. These targets were set up by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI). 

Now, I move on to the private sector banks. In the year 2001, only one bank could achieve the target of 18 per cent, while the other 30 banks had not met with any success. In the year 2002, only two private banks achieved the target of 18 per cent. Our hon. Finance Minister is trying to cover the whole picture in the figure of Rs. 1,05,500 crore to Rs. 1,08,000 crore. Whatever he wants to do, he has to do it district-wise and State-wise. So many banks are not going up to the mark of 18 per cent. This is on record. These sources are given by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI).

MR. DEPUTY-SPEAKER: Please conclude.

SHRI KINJARAPU YERRANNAIDU : I am giving the sources of RBI Bulletin. This is the ground reality.

My humble request, through you, Sir, to the hon. Finance Minister is that he should concentrate on agriculture. If he concentrates on agriculture, the economy will boost. This year, they want to achieve the target of 6.9 per cent of GDP. Today, agriculture contributes only 1.1 per cent. Last year, agriculture contributed 9 per cent. So, GDP has crossed more than 8 per cent. The National Common Minimum Programme sets the target to achieve 7 to 8 per cent. If you really want to achieve this target, you have to concentrate more on agriculture. Then and then only, you can achieve the target of 8 per cent. Otherwise, it is not possible to achieve the desired result. I will appreciate the Budget only when if you do any good of the farmer. This Budget is an anti-farmer Budget. Only the mere figures cannot help the farming community. If you stop this continuing and ongoing process of committing suicide by farmers and provide minimum support to them, then only the farmers will become happy.

Thank you very much for giving me this opportunity to put forward my views before this hon. House. 

MR. DEPUTY-SPEAKER: I would like to bring to the notice of the hon. Members that I have a long list of hon. Members who want to speak. So, I would request every hon. Member to try to complete his speech within five minutes. This is my humble request to hon. Members. Otherwise, You will not be able to finish this list in the whole night. I will allow only five minutes to each hon. Member.

SHRI KINJARAPU YERRANNAIDU : Sir, how many hon. Members want to speak?

MR. DEPUTY-SPEAKER: It is a long list.

* SHRI CHANDRA SEKHAR SAHU (BERHAMPUR - ORISSA): Sir, this Budget is pro poor and farmers friendly. Hon. Finance Minister while presenting the Budget has taken care of the common man as promised by the National Common Minimum Programme by the UPA Government. Sir, I do not want to repeat the points which my friends have already spoken. But, I want to remind my friends sitting on the other side that during the last seven years the NDA has taken the country to the path of capitalistic and pro rich and, therefore, poor became poorer. The programmes which have been started by Late Smt. Indira Gandhi and the dreams seen by Late Shri Rajiv Gandhi, were completely forgotten by the NDA followers. 

Sir, they claim that the country’s present good financial position is their contribution but if I remember, they have admitted in past that the present hon. Prime Minister is the real architect of the reforms. Now, under his leadership and under the guidance of hon. UPA Chairperson, Smt. Sonia Gandhi, during these last ten months "Bharat Nirman" has a starting. Sir, their feel good and India shining have been rejected by the people. But my friends on the other side are not in a position to digest the truth. Why at every point they want to disrupt the proceedings of the House?

Sir, coming to the Budget presented by hon. Finance Minister, it has taken care of all the sections of the people, especially, the common man.

*Speech was laid on the Table.

Sir, it is first time in the history of India that about more than eighty thousand crore of rupees have been provided for the rural development schemes so as to eradicate poverty and unemployment from the rural poor. Sir, this Budget has provision of new people friendly programmes such as National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme, National Rural Health Mission, Backward Regions Grant Fund, Micro Irrigation Project etc. To develop the infrastructure both in rural and urban areas it has given the new direction to the Budget by announcing programmes such as knowledge centres in every village, solving of drinking water problem in urban India as National Urban Renewal Million. 

Sir, as a whole it is a Budget which is growth oriented and shall definitely take India from developing towards a developed country as spoken by our hon. President of India that India shall be the World Super Power by 2020. 

Sir, I fully support the Budget presented by the hon. Finance Minister for the year 2005-2006.

SHRIMATI TEJASWINI SEE RAMESH (KANAKAPURA): I rise to support the UPA’s bold and brilliant Budget. The UPA Government presented a Budget keeping in mind the gender equality. I would like to congratulate the hon. Finance Minister, who is a dynamic leader, Shri P. Chidambaram Ji, for presenting this pro-people Budget guided by the hon. Prime Minister, Dr. Manmohan Singh Ji, and UPA’s Chairperson, Shrimati Sonia Gandhi Ji, and all the UPA leaders. The Budget won the hearts of millions of the Indian people, particularly, the farmers, labourers, children, youth and women, who will be going to be empowered. 

Let me first of all thank the hon. Finance Minister, Shri P. Chidambaram, for presenting a constructive, realistic and futuristic budget. This Budget also has continuity with the goals of the Budget presented by the hon. Minister in July 2004, that is, agriculture-oriented with a resolve to double agricultural credit in three years, launch a horticulture mission and a new weather insurance scheme.

The hon. Minister, in his speech presenting the Budget, mentioned about the need to work for the ‘greatest good to the greatest numbers’. With more than 60 per cent of the population living in the villages, it is imperative on the part of the Government to impart the ‘greatest good’ to these ‘greatest numbers’. Even if agricultural sector contributes only 21 per cent of the GDP of the country, as the hon. Minister has mentioned in his speech, it is necessary, that we re-focus on this sector. This also accords with the UPA Government’s agenda of National Common Minimum Programme, NCMP.

Giving a social touch to economic growth, the NCMP visualises that ‘the economy grows at least 7-8 per cent per year in a sustained manner over a decade and more, and in a manner that generates employment so that each family is assured of a safe and viable livelihood’. As the hon. Minister has mentioned in his speech, a ‘decisive intervention of the State in favour of the poor’ needs to be made to fulfil these objectives.

MR. DEPUTY-SPEAKER: If you want to read your speech, it will be better if you lay your speech on the Table of the House.

SHRIMATI TEJASWINI SEE RAMESH : I will do that, Sir.

One of the major problems in the Indian agricultural sector is the dwindling growth rates as compared to the other sectors of the economy. The economic surveys have indicated to the agricultural production decreasing for the past six to seven years, a decline of two per cent that led to an overall GDP growth below seven per cent. There has been some emphasis on the industrial and service sectors alone for some time now. Pandit Jawaharlal Nehruji clearly saw the linkage between agriculture and industrial sectors nevertheless. I would like to quote from his speech made in this House in December 1952:

"If our agricultural foundation is not strong then the industry we seek to build will not have a strong basis either. Apart from that, if our food front cracks up, everything will crack-up too."

In the initial decades, Panditji allocated as much as 22 per cent of the total Plan outlay for agriculture. These were mainly in the fields of irrigation, power, research and extension services. Despite problems related to famine and other factors, Independent India was able to achieve food self-sufficiency by the mid-1970s, though farm production slowed down in the recent period from 212 million tonnes in 2001-02 to 180 million tonnes. When we emphasise more, in the recent period, on industry and service sectors, we need to be reminded of this comprehensive approach of the 1950s and for the larger security of our economy.

Sir, due to time restriction I would like to lay rest of the part of my speech on the Table of the House. But before I conclude, I would like to emphasise that unless we protect the farmers of the nation with stable prices to their products, with quality power supply to their crops, with rural weightage marks to their children in higher education and employment, with crop insurance and health insurance, etc. we cannot strengthen this motherland.

I would humbly request the hon. Minister of Finance to waive off the loans with interest to the farmers, particularly farmers of the drought affected States. Sir, I come from the State of Karnataka where a lot of farmers committed suicides. I hope the hon. Minister will consider this demand considering the plight of the farmers of the drought affected States.

Sir, I would like to mention here that Kuvempu, a national Poet from Karnataka, who won the first Jnanpeeth Award dedicated a poem to the farmers called:

‘Uluva Yogya Nodali’

That means: 

"Look at the farmer, without any expectation he is serving the nation. Let the State emerge, let the State vanish, he will not leave his duty to produce the food grains to feed his fellow countrymen."

Let us not forget the farmer. Farmer is not a beggar, he is the backbone of the nation. As humble daughters and sons of this House, we must protect the farming community. 

With these words, I lay the remaining part of my speech on the Table of House. Thank you for giving me this opportunity, Sir. 

* If we have to overcome problems in the rural sector, it is imperative on our part to make efforts for sustained agricultural growth of at least 4 per cent per annum in the coming years. This calls for pro-active measures from the Government in enhancing budgetary allocations for irrigation facilities, rural infrastructure, employment generation, R&D in seeds, and improving easy but effective credit facilities to farmers.

*Speech was laid on the Table.

Overall public investments in the agriculture sector have declined in the 1990s to a mere Rs. 1,132 crore though private investments have come to the rescue of the Indian agriculture by raising investments up to Rs. 5,869 crore in the same period. Nevertheless, credit facilities in the rural areas are still hijacked by high-interest usurious groups. Indeed, the Reserve Bank of India admitted in 2002 that such public disbursement of credit declined from 15 per cent in 1980s to about 11 per cent. This needs to be evaluated and corrected. The CMP envisages that highest priority be given for investment in irrigation projects, as availability of water is a major issue determining agricultural production in India, given the vagaries of Monsoon. The plan is to bring additional one crore hectares under assured irrigation projects. This Budget provides for an increase of Rs. 14,000 crore in the total allocation for agriculture, irrigation and rural infrastructure. Our irrigation system has deteriorated over the years due to many factors including lack of investment.

Irrigation programmes along may not be able to overcome the problems. Experts have computed that, by 2020, water availability would drastically come down by 21 per cent, and one-third of India would be face to face with absolute water scarcity. In order to save precious water resources, we also need to focus on micro-irrigation projects as well. It needs to be pointed out that out of 27 million hectares which have the potential for micro-irrigation, so far only half-a-million hectares have been covered and the target for the next five years is just two million hectares. It is heartening to hear the hon. Minister’s budget speech on this subject: 

"1.2 million hectares have been covered under micro-irrigation so far, and the plan is to increase the coverage to 3 million hectares by the end of the Tenth Plan and to 14 million hectares by the end of the Eleventh Plan. Accordingly, I have provided Rs. 400 crore for promoting micro-irrigation in 2005-06".

As the task is urgent, we need to allocate more for these productive assets.

The UPA Government has made efforts to enhance of farm credit, more food-for-work programmes, and a mission on horticulture, restructuring farm insurance scheme, and revitalisation of rural co-operatives. The hon. Finance Minister has mentioned in his speech that credit was increased by about 30 per cent. Several experts have pointed to major flaws in the rural insurance schemes. These need to be carefully studies and rectified. The NABARD scheme of pre-development criterion for farmers, provision of crop insurance cover at nominal premium and other schemes need to be explored for effective implementation.

The area under certified seeds has increased from less than 500 hectares in 1962-63 to over 5 lakh hectares in 1999-2000, but is low as compared to other advanced countries. While overcoming problems related to transnational corporations’ entry into genetically modified crops, it is necessary for the Government to invest more in the public sector involved in the advanced seed projects, and enhance R&D facilities across the country. 

When we spend our precious resources on transforming agriculture from food grains to commercial crops, and reduction of subsidies as part of the WTO regulations, we need to learn from the Pakistan experience of food insecurity, in 80 out of 120 districts caused by introduction of corporate farming, reduction of subsidies and stopping the procurement of grains. Similar troubles stare at the neighbouring Chinese in their effort to transform the farm sector. 

On subsidies to the agriculture sector, it needs to be pointed out that these are necessary and that we need to oppose international pressures, in withdrawing them. According to a report of the International Food Policy research Institute September 2004, Indian farmers are losing nearly US $ 1.1 billion every year due to trade-distorting subsidies, which enrich United States and European Union farmers and traders. This practice is discriminatory because the US and EU spend nearly $ 300 billion subsidising their farmers (whereas we spend subsidies of about $ 1 billion only on our farmers) while pressurise us in cutting down these meager subsidies and opening up the agricultural sector for cheaper imports. It is in the right direction that in the Budget speech, the Finance Minister has mentioned that fertilizer subsidy has been increased to about Rs. 16,254 crore, though such amount is paltry and more needed to be allocated.

Unless we protect the farmers of the nation with stable prices for their produce, with quality power supply to their crops, with rural weightage marks to their children in higher education and employment, with crop insurance and health insurance, we cannot strengthen this Motherland.

Agriculture may not be a profitable occupation, still this humble farmer dedicates his life to feed his fellow countrymen. There is no match to this service. I appeal the Minister to waive off the loans with interest part in drought-affected States. 

Sir, we should respect and protect the interests of the farmers with pride. I will conclude my speech by remembering the poem written by the first Jnanapeeth-Award winner of Karnataka dedicated to farmers:

"Look at the farmer who ploughs the land,

Let the states emerge or vanish, he is not bothered

He is dedicated to feed the mouths of the fellows."

SHRI KINJARAPU YERRANNAIDU : Sir, I am also supporting the waiver of the loan as well as interest on the loan, as has been told by Shrimati Tejaswani Seeramesh.

SHRI BIR SINGH MAHATO (PURULIA): I rise to support this Budget 2005-06 as placed by the hon. Finance Minister. It is a balanced act. It tries to address the commitment made in the Common Minimum Programme. There are some welcome steps in the Budget. I welcome the proposal of the Finance Minister to create 1,88,165 Anganwadi Centres throughout the country. I also welcome the decision to cover drinking water in about 31,355 uncovered villages. I congratulate the Minister for the proposal regarding Total Sanitary Campaign Programme, which is going on in 452 districts. Now this Budget tries to cover all the districts throughout the country. I again welcome the proposal regarding creation of the Backward Region Grant Fund. 170 districts have been taken up through this Fund.

Regarding the widening of tax net, so far as I remember, the Standing Committee on Finance had made a number of concrete recommendations. I would like the hon. Minister of Finance to look into them.

The decision to de-reserve 180 items of small-scale industries would be detrimental to the rural and indigenous industries. This is against the commitment of the Common Minimum Programme.

There is no provision in the Budget regarding revival of public sector units and traditional industrial units and nothing has said regarding the revival of jute industry. Some support has been given to the sugar industry but no attention has been paid to the jute industry. One crore people in the eastern region depend on the jute industry. So, I would request the hon. Minister of Finance to give his attention to the revival of the jute industry.

SHRI B. VINOD KUMAR (HANAMKONDA): Thank you, Mr. Deputy Speaker, Sir. 

As a first time MP elected on the aspirations of the backward Telengana, I, on bhelaf of myself and on behalf of the telengana Rashtra Samiti, would like to congratulate the hon. Minister of Finance for devoting more than an hour of his Budget Speech to the components of the National Common Minimum Programme.

This Budget Speech, in character, justifies the mandate given by the people of this country to the United Progressive Alliance. This Budget reflects a remarkable social and rural sensitivity in its approach to the issues; and, fo this, I congratulate the hon. Prime Minister Dr. Manmohan Singh and the Chairperson of the UPA Shrimati Sonia Gandhi for providing the necessary directiona inputs.

Coming to the specific proposals of this Budget, the increased allocation for education and the rural mission from Rs. 8,420 crore to Rs. 10,280 crore, increased allocation for the Integrated Child Development Services from Rs. 1,623 crore to Rs. 3,142 crore, the increased allocation for the mid-day meal scheme from Rs. 1,675 crore to Rs. 3,010 crore and the move to create a non-lapsable fund are equally praiseworthy. The Budget Speech was also path breaking in providing an exclusive statement on the schemes particularly meant for the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes. Another praiseworthy initiative is the announcement of the new window of opportunity for students belonging to Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes for pursuing higher studies in institutes of excellence through the provision of a lot of scholarships but this scheme is to be impelemented immediately.

The United Progressive Alliance has gained power at the Centre by aggressively articulating the failure of the previous Government, particularly in the agricultural sector and by raising the aspirations of the Indian farmer. For this, the UPA has to redeem its pledge and commitment to the Indian farmer. I would lke to bring to your kind attention that the hon. Minister of Finance has himself admitted in a Press Conference at Hyderabad that only four crore farmers out of around 12 crore farmers in our country have access to institutional credit. This is a dismal and much less figure. I am very sorry to note that the hon. Minister of Finance has not given a serious reflection on this with any urgency to take bold initiatives.

Hence, I would request the hon. Minister of Finance to examine this subject and launch a "National Rural Credit Mission" to ensure rural credit to all the eligible farmers within next three years, as promised. Therefore, I once again humbly request the hon. Prime Minister, hon. Chairperson of the UPA, and hon. Minister of Finance to revisit this critical issue of Rural Credit. Hence, I would request, once again, the hon Minister of Finance to give a serious thougth on this issue.

Sir, because of paucity of time, I would just like to make one point here. I come from the backward region of Telengana and a backward district like Warangal. I welcome the initiatives of the hon. Minister of Finance on Backward Region Grant Fund for allocation of rs. 5,000 crore. But, I have a doubt. My district has been earlier covered under Rashtriya Sam Vikas Yojana which is being wound up. I would like to know whether my district is eligible for this Backward Region Grant Fund. It has to be clarified.

Lastly, coming from a rural constituency, it was a sweet music for me to hear the grand intention of Bharat Nirman with its six components relating to rural infrastrucutre. But I would request that one more component may be included, that is, Bharat Nirman Vision cannot be complete, unless land records in rural India are fully computerised by all the States….
